description.short_caption: Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain showing fungal hyphae in tissue.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image demonstrates fungal hyphae highlighted by a Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain. The hyphae are branching and septate, with a characteristic pink-magenta color against a lighter background. The stain enhances the polysaccharide components of the fungal cell walls, making them prominent. The tissue architecture is partially preserved, and there is no clear indication of the specific anatomical site.

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing a cavitary lesion in the right lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates a large cavitary lesion in the right lung, with thickened walls and surrounding consolidation. The left lung appears relatively normal. The mediastinum is midline, and no significant pleural effusion is visible. The findings are suggestive of a necrotizing infection or abscess.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right lung

description.short_caption: Gomori methenamine silver stain showing fungal hyphae.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gomori methenamine silver stain of a biopsy specimen. The stain highlights numerous branching fungal hyphae, which appear as black or dark brown structures against a lighter background. The hyphae exhibit septation and branching at acute angles, characteristic of certain fungal organisms. The staining technique is commonly used to identify fungal elements in tissue samples.
